description: Read an agent's most recent checkpoint without modifying anything: returns its ID, creation time (RFC3339), and the saved state as indented JSON, plus a message-turn count when messages were captured. Use at session start to detect and resume interrupted work; checkpoints are created with checkpoint_save. With no checkpoint, on_missing="error" (default) returns the historical not-found error; on_missing="empty" returns a successful {"found": false, "agent_id"} result. Errors stay prose-only for storage and daemon failures.

agent_id.description: The agent whose latest checkpoint to load.

on_missing.description: What to return when the agent has no checkpoint: "error" (default) keeps the historical not-found tool error; "empty" returns a successful {"found": false, "agent_id"} result.

name: checkpoint_resume
title: Load the latest checkpoint

description: Persist a snapshot of an agent's working state so a later session can pick the task back up with checkpoint_resume. Use before major refactors or when ending a session mid-task. Each save keeps its own ID and nothing is overwritten; checkpoint_resume returns the latest one. state must be a valid JSON object and is rejected otherwise. Returns a confirmation containing the new checkpoint ID.

state.description: Optional JSON object persisted with the checkpoint, e.g. {"branch": "main"}. Values that do not parse as an object are rejected.

name: checkpoint_save
title: Save a session checkpoint

description: Store one durable fact for an agent so future sessions can recall it. Use for conclusions worth keeping — decisions, preferences, gotchas — one atomic sentence per call, not transcripts or conversation logs. To correct or retire an existing fact use memory_reflect instead. Unpinned facts decay (30-day default half-life) and may eventually be pruned. Returns the agent and committed fact_id when supported.

agent_id.description: Stable agent identifier to associate this fact with.

confidence.description: Optional writer-declared confidence; omitted add stores legacy metadata, effectively inferred. This is not automated verification.

text.description: The fact to remember: one atomic, self-contained sentence.

name: memory_add
title: Store a durable fact

description: Declare that a term and another term mean the same thing in one agent's memory vocabulary, so later memory_search queries bridging the two reach the right facts. Use it when a search missed because your wording and the store's wording differ — the weak-match feedback block names this tool for exactly that case. Alias facts are never returned as memories and can be corrected with memory_reflect like any fact. Returns a confirmation naming the term and its equivalents.

agent_id.description: Stable agent identifier whose vocabulary this alias belongs to. Pass "__shared__" for project-wide memory.

equivalents.description: The words or phrases the store actually uses for the same thing; one or more.

term.description: The word or phrase as you would naturally write it in a query.

name: memory_alias
title: Teach the store a vocabulary alias

description: Curate an agent's memory: add a fact, update (supersede) an existing one, forget, pin or unpin against decay, or link two knowledge-graph nodes. Supply agent_id or deprecated alias agent: at least one is required at runtime, every supplied identity must be a non-empty string containing non-whitespace characters, and agent_id wins when both are valid. Use it mid-task when you notice a contradiction, finish a task, or learn a durable preference; for a brand-new fact memory_add is simpler. update requires the exact old fact text in target; forget, pin and unpin accept the fact via target or text, with target winning when both are set. Retirement leaves a tombstone that ordinary pruning can remove. Add/update report the committed fact_id when supported.

action.description: The self-curation action: add a new fact, update (supersede) an existing one, forget (retire with a tombstone), pin or unpin against decay, or link two knowledge-graph nodes.

agent.description: Deprecated alias of agent_id, accepted for compatibility. Supply this or agent_id; at least one is required at runtime. Every supplied identity must contain non-whitespace characters. agent_id wins when both are valid; namespace bytes are preserved.

agent_id.description: The agent whose memory to modify (canonical). Supply this or agent; at least one is required at runtime. Every supplied identity must contain non-whitespace characters. agent_id wins when both are valid; namespace bytes are preserved.

confidence.description: Writer-declared confidence, only for add/update. Omitted add is legacy inferred; omitted update is min(inferred, effective target confidence).

target.description: For update: the fact text to supersede. For forget/pin/unpin: the fact (or pass it via text). For link: the target node ID.

text.description: The fact text for add/update, the fact to forget or pin (alternative to target), or the source node ID for link.

name: memory_reflect
title: Curate your own memory

description: Search one agent's stored facts and return the most relevant ones ranked by hybrid recall (semantic + keyword + recency). Call once with your agent_id, then again with agent_id "__shared__" for project-wide conventions. Returns a numbered list with a count header, or a "No memories found" notice when nothing matches. Retired facts are excluded immediately. Results may carry a weak-match note naming the store's nearby vocabulary: reformulate once with those terms, and declare a lasting synonym with memory_alias instead of retrying synonyms blindly. To store new facts use memory_add; to correct, remove, or pin existing ones use memory_reflect. Open conflicts may carry review notices.

agent_id.description: Stable agent identifier, e.g. "graymatter-backend". Pass "__shared__" for project-wide memory.

confidence_weight.description: Optional finite preference weight in [0,0.5], default zero during opt-in rollout. Final score = base RRF * (1 + weight*c), c=1 verified, 0 inferred, -1 unverified. Zero retains an explicit filter.

explain.description: Set true to receive ranking receipts under `explained`. Each receipt carries signal ranks, fused RRF score, retention weight, age, and provenance. Recorded lineage includes exact content versions, typed relationships, and lineage status. The `supersedes` compatibility field includes legacy IDs reachable through retained tombstones. Explain uses the same ranking as ordinary search.

min_confidence.description: Optional minimum effective confidence, applied before ranking and top-k. Legacy empty labels are inferred; unknown historical labels are unverified. Any explicit filter suppresses graph hints without receipts.

query.description: Natural-language query; matching is hybrid (semantic + keyword + recency).

top_k.description: Optional cap on returned facts. Omitted or non-positive uses the store default.

name: memory_search
title: Search agent memory

description: Answer SEVERAL questions against one agent's memory in a single call, run concurrently. Use it whenever you hold more than one open question; use memory_search when you have exactly one. Put EVERY open question into ONE call: queries run in parallel server-side and splitting them costs a model round trip each. A query may come back with a weak-match note naming nearby vocabulary: reformulate those once with the suggested terms; lasting synonyms belong in memory_alias. Returns `merged`, a deduplicated best-first block ready to read where a fact answering several queries appears once, plus `per_query` for the individual lists. Ranking per query is identical to calling memory_search alone; this changes how many turns you spend, not what comes back. Open conflicts may carry review notices.

agent_id.description: Stable agent identifier, e.g. "graymatter-backend". Pass "__shared__" for project-wide memory.

confidence_weight.description: Optional finite preference weight in [0,0.5], default zero during opt-in rollout. Final score = base RRF * (1 + weight*c), c=1 verified, 0 inferred, -1 unverified. Zero retains an explicit filter.

min_confidence.description: Optional minimum effective confidence, applied before ranking and top-k. Legacy empty labels are inferred; unknown historical labels are unverified. Any explicit filter suppresses graph hints without receipts.

queries.description: The natural-language queries to answer, one per open question. Word each as you would for a single search; they are ranked independently and merged.

top_k.description: Optional cap on facts returned per query. Omitted or non-positive uses the store default.

name: memory_search_batch
title: Search agent memory with several queries at once
